text: Article · research post · Dwarkesh Podcast (Substack) Pretraining progress is mostly coming from data Dwarkesh Patel, Jerry Han (Dwarkesh Podcast) · published 8 September 2026 In one line: Training seven yearly open recipes (GPT-2 in 2019 to OLMo-2 in 2025) on seven yearly open corpora (OpenWebText to Ultra-FineWeb) at up to 1e19 FLOPs and scoring on OLMES (ten mostly multiple-choice tasks, at least three seeds per curve), the 2025 corpus matched the 2019 pair's score with 12.0x less compute and the 2025 recipe with 3.7x less; together they saved 15x, a third of the product, though score gains in a one-seed grid are 88% additive.
label: core
key: article · research post · dwarkesh podcast (substack)

text: The evidence, judged . read it (12 min) · discussion (1,780 points, 52 comments on 27 November 2026) · discussion (235 points, 19 comments on 27 November 2026) The idea in one sentence: train every year's open model recipe on every year's open corpus at small budgets, ask how much less compute each newer ingredient needs to match the 2019 pair's benchmark score, and the corpora from 2019 to 2025 turn out to be worth 12.0 times the compute and the recipes 3.7 times; together they are worth 15 times, not 45, because the two gains overlap.
